subject: Per-token rebate and marketplace routing — BlueWave Analytics
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Holt <jared.holt@bluewave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Per-token rebate and marketplace routing — BlueWave Analytics

Hi Jared — great to talk today. As promised, a short note to align on the two pricing paths we discussed and the open questions you flagged around marketplace metering vs direct billing. High level: you want equivalent net economics whether you buy directly from Redwood or via AWS Marketplace, and want predictable commit crediting.

Two options we typically present:
- Direct contract (hosted API): usage-based per-token billing with a 12-month commit and volume discount tiers. This gives us direct metering and easier commit reconciliation.
- Marketplace purchase (AWS/GCP): purchase via the marketplace channel. Marketplace charges a platform commission (typically 8–15% depending on program), which affects list pricing and how discounts are applied. Marketplace metering can be used for commit crediting, but terms vary across clouds and sometimes require an addendum.

Open items for your team (and mine):
1) Does BlueWave need committed usage to be tracked by marketplace metering, or is a direct contract (with marketplace procurement as a billing path) acceptable?
2) If marketplace is required, do you expect the marketplace list price to be the source of truth for discounts, or do you want Redwood to absorb the marketplace commission?
3) Timing: you mentioned a January-ish production go-live; do you prefer a ramped commit (3–6 months) or flat monthly commit?

Attached: Redwood_pricing_model_v2.xlsx (simple model showing per-token math), aws_marketplace_fee_layout.pdf (vendor-facing fee schedules). I copied Marcus and Neha to lock down the numbers and Vanessa for marketplace/legal ops.

Proposed next step: I can send two concrete quotes (direct vs marketplace) with net-effective per-million token prices and a suggested marketplace offset if needed. Can we lock a call Friday 4/16 to review?

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Jared Holt <jared.holt@bluewave.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-token rebate and marketplace routing — BlueWave Analytics

Sergio — thanks for the summary. A couple quick clarifications from procurement/engineering:
- Important: we need marketplace metering to count toward any commit. Our finance team requires a Marketplace invoice trail.
- We prefer a flat monthly commit (easier for forecasting) but would accept a 3-month ramp if the economics are better.
- Can you provide a single net $/M-token figure for each path (direct vs marketplace) so our CFO can compare?

If marketplace metering is a blocker, we can discuss whether to sign a direct agreement and still have procurement buy via marketplace — but that may complicate their internal approval.

Can you include whether Dedicated/Dedicated-like usage (if we later add reserved capacity) counts toward the same commit bucket?

Jared
Jared Holt
Head of Procurement, BlueWave Analytics
jared.holt@bluewave.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Per-token rebate and marketplace routing — BlueWave Analytics

Sergio / team — quick pass on the math and options so we can draft quotes. Assumptions pulled from the model: BlueWave expected 12M monthly tokens in steady state (ramp to that in 3 months).

Baseline list price (hosted API): $0.0008 / token (list)
Direct 15% volume discount --> net = $0.00068 / token
That equals $680 per million tokens.

Marketplace math (assume AWS marketplace commission 12%):
- If we keep list = $0.0008, AWS takes 12% -> Redwood nets $0.000704 -> after 15% discount applied on list? (depends on whether discount is applied pre- or post-commission). Practically we need to raise list to ~ $0.00077 to net the same $0.00068. Example: list $0.00077 * (1 - 12%) = $0.0006776.

Options to offer BlueWave (recommended):
A) Direct contract: 12-month, $1.2M committed spend (equiv. ~1.76B tokens annual), flat monthly commit. Net $/M-token = $680.
B) Marketplace: List priced to yield same net to Redwood; to match net economics we set marketplace list commit = $1.35M (this accounts for commissions). Redwood provides a $150k marketplace offset credit applied to invoices over first 3 months to smooth approval friction.

Other considerations:
- Counting Dedicated tokens: yes, can be bundled if you include a cross-product clause in the SOW that says "Committed usage may include hosted API and Greenwood Dedicated endpoints" (subject to min token equivalency conversion). Need legal to sign off on that language — Vanessa, note for legal ops.
- Metering: AWS metering can be used to validate monthly consumption but we still recommend a direct reconciliation line on our invoices for transparency.

I'll draft the two quote templates and a one-page explanation for procurement.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Pricing Ops, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Per-token rebate and marketplace routing — BlueWave Analytics

Thanks Marcus — useful breakdown. A few legal/finance asks before we send to the customer:
1) Marketplace metering: we can accept AWS metering as evidence of consumption, but procurement needs an annex that explicitly states "Marketplace-metered usage will count toward Customer's committed usage under the Agreement." Vanessa, please prepare that annex and flag any marketplace program acceptance windows or certification requirements.
2) Ramp clause: recommend a 3-month ramp to target with a 9-month tail to avoid early-termination cliffs (i.e., if usage undershoots, prorated reconciliation but capped at 30% of committed).
3) Marketplace offset: any credit we give to offset marketplace commission should be explicitly limited to the first 90 days and tied to invoice offsets, not to list price adjustments. Keeps our long-term list clean.

Finance: please model cashflow timing of the $150k offset vs discounted list to ensure ARR recognition lines up — cc'ing Vanessa for compliance.

If all good, Sergio please share the two quote PDFs and a one-pager with the finance math.

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Director, Sales Finance, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Holt <jared.holt@bluewave.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Per-token rebate and marketplace routing — BlueWave Analytics

Jared — thanks for the quick replies and for clarifying procurement's marketplace preference. Below is a concise proposal for BlueWave to review. I attached the pricing PDFs and the model.

Option 1 — Direct Redwood Contract (recommended for simplest reconciliation)
- 12-month commitment: $1.2M committed spend (flat monthly commitment).
- Net effective price: $680 / M-tokens (equiv. $0.00068 / token) after 15% volume discount.
- Dedicated usage can be included if SOW cross-product clause is present.

Option 2 — AWS Marketplace Purchase (procurement preferred)
- Marketplace list commitment: $1.35M (accounts for ~12% AWS commission).
- Redwood marketplace offset credit: $150k applied across invoices in the first 90 days to match net economics to Option 1.
- Metering: AWS metering will be accepted as evidence of usage for commit reconciliation; however, commit language must be added to the agreement annex (see attached annex template).

Next steps / asks:
- Jared: confirm which option you prefer so we can prepare quote PDFs.
- BlueWave procurement: confirm whether a 3-month ramp -> steady-state is acceptable or if you want flat monthly.
- Vanessa/Legal: finalize annex wording that marketplace metering counts toward committed usage.
- I will send DocuSign for the chosen quote and the annex once we confirm. Link: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcd-efgh-1234

Call: can we meet Fri 4/16 10:00 PT to finalize?

Best,
Sergio
